answer: An agent market grants one bid per auction for every $100 locked in a contract for 30 days, rather than one bid per account. Whether agents trade sable pelts or rent a jetty, a ripple of new identities creates no extra bidding power: each additional bid needs another deposit. An attacker seeking 10,000 bids must immobilize $1 million for a month, sacrificing liquidity and interest even if every identity is free.
